narrative_purpose: Shows why point-to-point memory retrieval is not evidence of a global conscious workspace: one Na'vi opens one bright local path at a sacred tree while the immense surrounding root web remains in separate dim pockets rather than igniting together.
subject: A Na'vi kneels at the hanging tendrils of a sacred willow-like tree and joins a queue to one tendril. From that single contact, one narrow bright path runs down the trunk and through the roots to one small distant cluster holding a faint ancestral silhouette. All around it, an enormous underground mesh extends to many other clusters, but those regions remain dim, separate, and unlit; there is no planet-wide flash and no central glowing brain.
scene: Night at a sacred tree with the soil shown in cross-section, one local memory route illuminated inside a far larger dormant network.
camera: Wide side-on cutaway holding the kneeling figure, the tree, and the branching underground mesh in one frame.
light: The single accessed route glows bright cyan from the living contact to one memory pocket; the rest of the network stays in deep teal shadow.
palette: Cool network tones with one restrained magenta trace inside the ancestral memory pocket; no broad warm illumination.
style: Painterly speculative-biology naturalist cutaway, observed and anatomical rather than mystical poster art.
detail_level: Crisp on the local contact and one illuminated route, increasingly soft and dim across the unused network.
composition: Na'vi and tree on the left third, selected memory pocket on the right third, dormant network spanning the lower frame with dark space above and between.
consistency_notes: Only one point-to-point route may be bright. The larger mesh must visibly remain partitioned into dim local pockets, which is the teaching contrast.
negative_prompt: no text, no lettering, no labels, no arrows, no planet-wide ignition, no central deity face, no photographic or 3D-render look, no lens flare, no neon UI
